result.title: Checking the Checkers: A Synthesis of Verifier Noise and Robustness in RLVR
result.comment: Accepted at the International Conference on Artificial Intelligence Centric Systems, Services, and Applications (AISSA 2026)
result.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become a principal recipe for improving the reasoning of large language models (LLMs). It rests on the assumption that the checker scoring each response is itself correct. In practice, rule-based checkers reject correct answers in unexpected formats, unit tests accept incorrect programs, and LLM judges can be led to approve empty or adversarial responses. This work surveys 58 studies that measure, analyze, or mitigate such verifier errors. We ask what errors verifiers make, how they affect training, which mitigations work against which errors, and how the findings extend to self-generated, rubric- and judge-based, and verifier-free rewards. The evidence suggests that the structure of an error matters more than its rate. Random errors mostly slow learning, though under a fixed budget or KL regularization they also lower final accuracy. False positives that the policy can learn to trigger can cause plateaus or collapse, sometimes even with a low initial error rate. Whether a verifier wrongly rejects or accepts depends on what it checks and who built it, not on its family. Its errors shift as the policy improves, and most mitigations have been tested against only one kind of error. We compile the findings into comparison tables, reconcile apparent conflicts in the literature, and propose a reporting protocol to make future results comparable.

AI.brief_summary: 综述 58 项研究，梳理 RLVR 中规则检查器、单元测试与 LLM 评判等验证器的错误类型、对训练的影响及缓解手段，并整理对比表与报告协议。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽为纯文本 RLVR 综述，但其关于「错误结构比错误率更重要」、可被策略触发的假阳性导致plateau或塌缩的结论，可供核查 latent 推理训练中轨迹监督质量、奖励劫持与贡献分配问题。
